\section[o raciocínio]{o raciocínio — the reasoning, the train of thought}

\label{lesson:PT-C346-raciocinio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the criticism, then the Portuguese for to weigh up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o raciocínio}
\textbf{o raciocínio} — \textquotedblleft{}the reasoning, the train of thought\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O teu raciocínio está certo, mas a conta está errada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Your reasoning is right, but the sum is wrong.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Raciocinar} — to reason.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{raciocínio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ratiōcinium} \textquotedblleft{}a reckoning, a computation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{ratiō} \textquotedblleft{}reckoning, reason\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o raciocínio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o raciocínio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o raciocínio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the criticism, then the Portuguese for to weigh up, then say \emph{o raciocínio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o raciocínio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The reasoning, the train of thought\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[deduzir]{deduzir — to deduce; to deduct}

\label{lesson:PT-C346-deduzir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to weigh up, then the Portuguese for the reasoning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: deduzir}
\textbf{deduzir} — \textquotedblleft{}to deduce; to deduct\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pelas malas, deduzi que eles iam viajar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{From the suitcases, I deduced that they were going to travel.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{conduzir}: \emph{deduzo, deduzes, deduz}. Also to deduct a sum.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{deduzir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēdūcere} \textquotedblleft{}to lead down, to lead away, to derive\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{dē} and \emph{dūcere} \textquotedblleft{}to lead\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{deduzir}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to weigh up, then the Portuguese for the reasoning, then say \emph{deduzir} again
\end{itemize}

\section[concluir]{concluir — to conclude; to finish}

\label{lesson:PT-C346-concluir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the reasoning, then the Portuguese for to deduce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: concluir}
\textbf{concluir} — \textquotedblleft{}to conclude; to finish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois de ler tudo, concluí que ele tinha razão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After reading everything, I concluded that he was right.}
\end{quote}

Also to finish: \emph{concluir o curso} — to finish the degree.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{concluir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{conclūdere} \textquotedblleft{}to shut up, to close, to end\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{con-} and \emph{claudere} \textquotedblleft{}to shut\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a conclusão]{a conclusão — the conclusion}

\label{lesson:PT-C346-conclusao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to deduce, then the Portuguese for to conclude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a conclusão}
\textbf{a conclusão} — \textquotedblleft{}the conclusion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Chegámos todos à mesma conclusão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We all reached the same conclusion.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Em conclusão} — in conclusion.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{conclusão} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{conclūsiō} \textquotedblleft{}a shutting up, a conclusion\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{conclūdere}, built on \emph{claudere} \textquotedblleft{}to shut\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o critério]{o critério — the criterion}

\label{lesson:PT-C346-criterio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to conclude, then the Portuguese for the conclusion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o critério}
\textbf{o critério} — \textquotedblleft{}the criterion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Qual é o critério para escolher os jogadores?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{What is the criterion for choosing the players?}
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{os critérios}. \emph{Com critério} — with good judgement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{critério} is a learned word from Greek \emph{krit\'{\={e}}rion} \textquotedblleft{}a means of judging, a standard\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{krínein} \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{}; compare Latin \emph{criticus} \textquotedblleft{}capable of judging\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
